newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to let Conoco to drill in Utah - Post.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to let Conoco to drill in Utah - Post.

text.p: The U.S. Interior Department's Bureau of Land Management is poised to allow DuPont Co unit Conoco to drill for oil in the heart of a federal lease in a national monument in Utah, the Washington Post reported Wednesday.

The newspaper said officials in the Interior Department were betting that dozens of oil and gas leases that predated creation of the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument by President Bill Clinton last September were virtually worthless.
Conoco has estimated the area could hold more than a hundred million barrels of oil reserves.

The federal officials believe the odds are heavily in their favour that Conoco's exploratory wells will come up dry and that the oil giant and others holding "valid existing rights" to drill for oil on the 108,000 acres of federal land will allow their 10-year leases to expire, the Post said.
Over the last four or five decades, dozens of exploratory holes have been drilled without success in what is now the monument area, Interior Department officials said.
Conoco in March won approval from Utah to drill on a state lease in the area and is close to beginning drilling.

John Leshy, the department's solicitor and other officials told the Post Conoco's exploratory drilling would have little appreciable impact on the natural resource values of the Kaiparowits Plateau, particularly when compared with a huge coal mine that had been proposed and which spurred Clinton's creation of the monument.
Conoco officials have previously said they would be careful about drilling efforts in the protected area.

The Washington Post quoted Bob Irelan, Conoco's regional director for exploration and production, who said the company will be drilling deeper than previous exploratory attempts and still believes "there's a huge source."
"This is big enough you just can't walk away from it," Irelan told the newspaper. "It could be billions of barrels of oil."
